en.setting: Dunne Harbour sits in a granite cove facing west, where the slipway drops steeply and the sea wall holds back spring tides. The fishing fleet dominates the local economy, and a marine survey has been measuring stock levels that the fleet owner would rather not see published. At low slack, the sea cave at the base of the headland opens for forty minutes.
en.crime: Ellen Cross, a marine researcher, was found in the sea cave at dawn after the tide receded. Her sample jars sat beside her, her research cabin stood empty on the cliff above, and the forty-minute window of low slack had become her tomb.

suspects.name: Piers Dunne
suspects.intro: Fleet owner whose boats exceeded the annual quota by three hundred tonnes, his oilskin dry but his boots carrying a tide line.

suspects.name: Gill Rowan
suspects.intro: Dunne's lead crewman who knows the cave passages, his salt-stained jacket hanging in the chandlery.

suspects.name: The Harbour Master
suspects.intro: Signed the daily logbook and controlled slipway access, his entries for the night unusually brief.

suspects.name: Malcolm Crewe
suspects.intro: Fish market operator who handled the catch manifests, his fuel receipts showing a boat trip that night.

suspects.name: Fiona Cross
suspects.intro: The victim's sister, who argued with Dunne over access permits, her boots carrying salt from the breakwater.

suspects.name: Coastguard Bell
suspects.intro: Patrolled the coast path and logged vessel movements, his camera housing found empty in the research cabin.

suspects.name: Dr Anne Webb
suspects.intro: Supervised the marine survey whose report was due at the ministry by month's end.

es.setting: El Puerto Dunne se asienta en una ensenada de granito orientada al oeste, donde la rampa cae en pendiente y el dique contiene las mareas vivas. La flota pesquera domina la economia local, y un estudio marino ha estado midiendo niveles de poblacion que el dueno de la flota preferiria no ver publicados. En la calma baja, la cueva marina al pie del promontorio se abre durante cuarenta minutos.
es.crime: Ellen Cross, una investigadora marina, fue encontrada en la cueva marina al amanecer tras retirarse la marea. Sus frascos de muestras estaban a su lado, su cabana de investigacion vacia en el acantilado, y la ventana de cuarenta minutos de calma baja se habia convertido en su tumba.

suspects.name: Piers Dunne
suspects.intro: Dueno de la flota cuyos barcos excedieron la cuota anual en trescientas toneladas, su impermeable seco pero sus botas con una marca de marea.

suspects.name: Gill Rowan
suspects.intro: Tripulante principal de Dunne que conoce los pasajes de la cueva, su chaqueta manchada de sal colgando en la tienda nautica.

suspects.name: El Capitan de Puerto
suspects.intro: Firmo el libro diario y controlaba el acceso a la rampa, sus anotaciones de esa noche inusualmente breves.

suspects.name: Malcolm Crewe
suspects.intro: Operador del mercado de pescado que manejaba los manifiestos de captura, sus recibos de combustible mostrando un viaje en barco esa noche.

suspects.name: Fiona Cross
suspects.intro: La hermana de la victima, que discutio con Dunne sobre permisos de acceso, sus botas con sal del rompeolas.

suspects.name: Guardacostas Bell
suspects.intro: Patrullaba el sendero costero y registraba movimientos de embarcaciones, la carcasa de su camara encontrada vacia en la cabana de investigacion.

suspects.name: Dra. Anne Webb
suspects.intro: Supervisaba el estudio marino cuyo informe debia entregarse al ministerio a fin de mes.

fr.setting: Le Port Dunne se niche dans une crique de granit face a l'ouest, ou la cale descend abruptement et la digue retient les marees de vive-eau. La flotte de peche domine l'economie locale, et une etude marine mesure les niveaux de stocks que le proprietaire de la flotte prefererait ne pas voir publies. A l'etale de basse mer, la grotte marine au pied du promontoire s'ouvre pendant quarante minutes.
fr.crime: Ellen Cross, chercheuse marine, a ete retrouvee dans la grotte marine a l'aube apres le retrait de la maree. Ses bocaux d'echantillons etaient a cote d'elle, sa cabane de recherche vide sur la falaise au-dessus, et la fenetre de quarante minutes d'etale de basse mer etait devenue sa tombe.

suspects.name: Piers Dunne
suspects.intro: Proprietaire de la flotte dont les bateaux ont depasse le quota annuel de trois cents tonnes, son ciret sec mais ses bottes portant une ligne de maree.

suspects.name: Gill Rowan
suspects.intro: Premier equipier de Dunne qui connait les passages de la grotte, sa veste tachee de sel accrochee dans la shipchandler.

suspects.name: Le Capitaine du Port
suspects.intro: A signe le journal quotidien et controlait l'acces a la cale, ses entrees pour la nuit inhabituellement breves.

suspects.name: Malcolm Crewe
suspects.intro: Exploitant du marche aux poissons qui gerait les manifestes de capture, ses recus de carburant montrant une sortie en bateau cette nuit-la.

suspects.name: Fiona Cross
suspects.intro: La soeur de la victime, qui s'est disputee avec Dunne au sujet des permis d'acces, ses bottes portant du sel de la digue.

suspects.name: Garde-cote Bell
suspects.intro: Patrouillait le sentier cotier et enregistrait les mouvements de navires, le boitier de son appareil photo trouve vide dans la cabane de recherche.

suspects.name: Dr Anne Webb
suspects.intro: Supervisait l'etude marine dont le rapport devait etre remis au ministere avant la fin du mois.

physical_evidence.en: Keel scrapes on the slipway matched Dunne's boat hull. The mooring rope in the sea cave had been cut, not worn through, and the anchor chain was shortened to prevent escape. Ellen Cross's sample jars sat beside her in the cave, and her research cabin stood empty on the cliff above.
physical_evidence.es: Las marcas de quilla en la rampa coincidian con el casco del barco de Dunne. La cuerda de amarre en la cueva marina habia sido cortada, no desgastada, y la cadena de ancla acortada para impedir la huida. Los frascos de muestras de Ellen Cross estaban junto a ella en la cueva, y su cabana de investigacion permanecia vacia en el acantilado.
physical_evidence.fr: Les raclures de quille sur la cale correspondaient a la coque du bateau de Dunne. L'amarre dans la grotte marine avait ete coupee, pas usee, et la chaine d'ancre raccourcie pour empecher toute fuite. Les bocaux d'echantillons d'Ellen Cross etaient a cote d'elle dans la grotte, et sa cabane de recherche etait vide sur la falaise au-dessus.

witness_testimony.en: Gill Rowan knew the cave passages and placed Dunne at the harbour after dark. The harbour master's logbook entries for the night were unusually brief. Malcolm Crewe's fuel receipts showed a boat trip that night, and Coastguard Bell's camera housing was found empty in the research cabin.
witness_testimony.es: Gill Rowan conocia los pasajes de la cueva y situo a Dunne en el puerto despues del anochecer. Las anotaciones del libro del capitan de puerto para esa noche eran inusualmente breves. Los recibos de combustible de Malcolm Crewe mostraban un viaje en barco esa noche, y la carcasa de la camara del Guardacostas Bell fue encontrada vacia en la cabana de investigacion.
witness_testimony.fr: Gill Rowan connaissait les passages de la grotte et a place Dunne au port apres la tombee de la nuit. Les entrees du journal du capitaine du port pour la nuit etaient inhabituellement breves. Les recus de carburant de Malcolm Crewe montraient une sortie en bateau cette nuit-la, et le boitier de l'appareil photo du Garde-cote Bell a ete trouve vide dans la cabane de recherche.

financial_trail.en: Dunne's fleet exceeded the annual quota by three hundred tonnes. The falsified landing records in the fish market showed catches that never matched the manifests. Ellen Cross's marine survey would have revoked his fleet's licence, and Dr Anne Webb's report was due at the ministry by month's end.
financial_trail.es: La flota de Dunne excedio la cuota anual en trescientas toneladas. Los registros de desembarque falsificados en el mercado de pescado mostraban capturas que nunca coincidian con los manifiestos. El estudio marino de Ellen Cross habria revocado la licencia de su flota, y el informe de la Dra. Anne Webb debia entregarse al ministerio a fin de mes.
financial_trail.fr: La flotte de Dunne avait depasse le quota annuel de trois cents tonnes. Les registres de debarquement falsifies au marche aux poissons montraient des prises qui ne correspondaient jamais aux manifestes. L'etude marine d'Ellen Cross aurait revoque la licence de sa flotte, et le rapport du Dr Anne Webb devait etre remis au ministere avant la fin du mois.

emotional_tells.en: Dunne's oilskin was dry but his boots carried a tide line that placed him at the water's edge. Fiona Cross argued with Dunne over access permits, her voice carrying across the harbour. The harbour master wrote his briefest log entry on the night a woman died in his cove.
emotional_tells.es: El impermeable de Dunne estaba seco pero sus botas llevaban una marca de marea que lo situaba al borde del agua. Fiona Cross discutio con Dunne sobre permisos de acceso, su voz resonando por el puerto. El capitan de puerto escribio su anotacion mas breve la noche que una mujer murio en su ensenada.
emotional_tells.fr: Le ciret de Dunne etait sec mais ses bottes portaient une ligne de maree qui le placait au bord de l'eau. Fiona Cross s'est disputee avec Dunne au sujet des permis d'acces, sa voix portant a travers le port. Le capitaine du port a ecrit son entree de journal la plus breve la nuit ou une femme est morte dans sa crique.

cold_case_physical.en: The sea cave flooded and drained with each tide, washing away whatever the granite walls had witnessed. The cut mooring rope was taken by the current. The slipway was scraped by keels that left no names, and Ellen Cross's sample jars sat on a shelf in an empty cabin, measuring nothing.
cold_case_physical.es: La cueva marina se inundaba y drenaba con cada marea, lavando lo que los muros de granito habian presenciado. La cuerda de amarre cortada fue llevada por la corriente. La rampa fue raspada por quillas que no dejaban nombres, y los frascos de muestras de Ellen Cross se quedaron en un estante de una cabana vacia, sin medir nada.
cold_case_physical.fr: La grotte marine se remplissait et se vidait a chaque maree, emportant tout ce que les murs de granit avaient vu. L'amarre coupee a ete emportee par le courant. La cale etait raclee par des quilles qui ne laissaient aucun nom, et les bocaux d'echantillons d'Ellen Cross restaient sur une etagere dans une cabane vide, ne mesurant rien.

cold_case_financial.en: The marine survey was filed incomplete, and the ministry extended the quota deadline without comment. The falsified landing records were rewritten, and Dunne Harbour continued to land its catch by night. The fleet licence was renewed, and the three hundred tonnes of excess catch vanished into the books like the tide into the granite cove.
cold_case_financial.es: El estudio marino fue archivado como incompleto, y el ministerio extendio el plazo de cuotas sin comentarios. Los registros de desembarque falsificados fueron reescritos, y el Puerto Dunne continuo desembarcando su captura de noche. La licencia de la flota fue renovada, y las trescientas toneladas de captura excedente desaparecieron en los libros como la marea en la ensenada de granito.
cold_case_financial.fr: L'etude marine a ete classee incomplete, et le ministere a prolonge le delai de quota sans commentaire. Les registres de debarquement falsifies ont ete reecrits, et le Port Dunne a continue de debarquer ses prises de nuit. La licence de la flotte a ete renouvelee, et les trois cents tonnes de captures excedentaires ont disparu dans les livres comme la maree dans la crique de granit.

all_strong.en: Piers Dunne launched a boat in the dark, cut the mooring rope to strand Ellen Cross in the cave, and let the tide do the rest. Three hundred tonnes of excess catch, falsified landing records, and a marine survey that would have ended his fleet's licence — the evidence flowed in as surely as the water that filled the cave at 02:54. The keel scrapes on the slipway, the shortened anchor chain, the disabled engine ignition: each piece locked together like the tidal tables that governed the forty-minute window. The sea gave up its proof at dawn, and the harbour had its reckoning.
all_strong.es: Piers Dunne lanzo un barco en la oscuridad, corto la cuerda de amarre para dejar a Ellen Cross varada en la cueva, y dejo que la marea hiciera el resto. Trescientas toneladas de captura excedente, registros de desembarque falsificados, y un estudio marino que habria revocado la licencia de su flota — las pruebas llegaron tan seguramente como el agua que lleno la cueva a las 02:54. Las marcas de quilla en la rampa, la cadena de ancla acortada, el encendido del motor deshabilitado: cada pieza encajaba como las tablas de mareas que gobernaban la ventana de cuarenta minutos. El mar entrego sus pruebas al amanecer, y el puerto tuvo su ajuste de cuentas.
all_strong.fr: Piers Dunne a mis un bateau a l'eau dans l'obscurite, coupe l'amarre pour laisser Ellen Cross echouee dans la grotte, et laisse la maree faire le reste. Trois cents tonnes de captures excedentaires, des registres de debarquement falsifies, et une etude marine qui aurait mis fin a la licence de sa flotte — les preuves sont arrivees aussi surement que l'eau qui a rempli la grotte a 02h54. Les raclures de quille sur la cale, la chaine d'ancre raccourcie, le demarreur du moteur desactive : chaque piece s'emboitait comme les tables de marees qui gouvernaient la fenetre de quarante minutes. La mer a livre ses preuves a l'aube, et le port a eu ses comptes.

who_strong_rest_weak.en: Dunne's name rode every wave that came ashore that morning. His fleet, his quota, his harbour — the motive was as wide as the cove. But the tidal window left no footprints, the cut rope looked like wear, and the disabled engine could not be pinned to any particular hand. He was arrested because the harbour economy began and ended with his name, and that was enough for a town that had already made up its mind. The conviction floated on inference, not evidence.
who_strong_rest_weak.es: El nombre de Dunne cabalgaba cada ola que llego a la orilla esa manana. Su flota, su cuota, su puerto — el motivo era tan amplio como la ensenada. Pero la ventana de mareas no dejo huellas, la cuerda cortada parecia desgaste, y el motor deshabilitado no pudo ser atribuido a ninguna mano en particular. Fue arrestado porque la economia del puerto empezaba y terminaba con su nombre, y eso fue suficiente para un pueblo que ya habia tomado su decision. La condena floto sobre inferencia, no sobre evidencia.
who_strong_rest_weak.fr: Le nom de Dunne chevauchait chaque vague qui a atteint le rivage ce matin-la. Sa flotte, son quota, son port — le mobile etait aussi large que la crique. Mais la fenetre de maree n'a laisse aucune empreinte, la corde coupee ressemblait a de l'usure, et le moteur desactive n'a pu etre attribue a aucune main en particulier. Il a ete arrete parce que l'economie du port commencait et finissait par son nom, et cela a suffi pour une ville qui avait deja pris sa decision. La condamnation flottait sur l'inference, pas sur les preuves.

wrong_accusation.en: The wrong fisherman was netted, and Piers Dunne's boats put out at dawn as they always had. The quota records were rewritten, the survey report delayed, and Ellen Cross's sample jars were shelved in a research cabin that the ministry never inspected. The harbour economy continued to exceed its limits, the sea cave flooded and drained with each tide, and the truth lay at the bottom of it all, buried under salt and granite and forty minutes of rising water.
wrong_accusation.es: El pescador equivocado fue atrapado en la red, y los barcos de Piers Dunne zarparon al amanecer como siempre. Los registros de cuotas fueron reescritos, el informe del estudio retrasado, y los frascos de muestras de Ellen Cross archivados en una cabana de investigacion que el ministerio nunca inspeccion. La economia del puerto siguio excediendo sus limites, la cueva marina se inundaba y drenaba con cada marea, y la verdad yacia en el fondo de todo, enterrada bajo sal y granito y cuarenta minutos de agua creciente.
wrong_accusation.fr: Le mauvais pecheur a ete pris dans le filet, et les bateaux de Piers Dunne sont sortis a l'aube comme toujours. Les registres de quotas ont ete reecrits, le rapport d'etude retarde, et les bocaux d'echantillons d'Ellen Cross ranges dans une cabane de recherche que le ministere n'a jamais inspectee. L'economie portuaire a continue de depasser ses limites, la grotte marine se remplissait et se vidait a chaque maree, et la verite gisait au fond de tout cela, ensevelie sous le sel et le granit et quarante minutes d'eau montante.

cold_case.en: The tide came and went, and the case went with it. Ellen Cross's research was filed incomplete, the marine survey was never published, and the ministry extended the quota deadline without comment. Dunne Harbour continued to land its catch by night, the slipway scraped by keels that left no names, and the sea cave opened and closed with each cycle as if it had never held anyone at all. The sample jars sat on a shelf in an empty cabin, measuring nothing.
cold_case.es: La marea iba y venia, y el caso se fue con ella. La investigacion de Ellen Cross fue archivada como incompleta, el estudio marino nunca fue publicado, y el ministerio extendio el plazo de cuotas sin comentarios. El Puerto Dunne continuo desembarcando su captura de noche, la rampa raspada por quillas que no dejaban nombres, y la cueva marina se abria y cerraba con cada ciclo como si nunca hubiera contenido a nadie. Los frascos de muestras se quedaron en un estante de una cabana vacia, sin medir nada.
cold_case.fr: La maree allait et venait, et l'affaire est partie avec elle. La recherche d'Ellen Cross a ete classee incomplete, l'etude marine n'a jamais ete publiee, et le ministere a prolonge le delai de quota sans commentaire. Le Port Dunne a continue de debarquer ses prises de nuit, la cale raclee par des quilles qui ne laissaient aucun nom, et la grotte marine s'ouvrait et se fermait a chaque cycle comme si elle n'avait jamais retenu personne. Les bocaux d'echantillons restaient sur une etagere dans une cabane vide, ne mesurant rien.

lucky_guess.en: Dunne's name washed ashore on the morning tide like driftwood — present, plausible, but proving nothing on its own. The tide line on his boots, the fuel receipt in the chandlery, the harbour log overwritten in darker ink: each detail suggested without confirming. He was charged because the cove belonged to him and the dead woman had threatened his livelihood. The sea, as always, offered no testimony, and the verdict rested on the rhythm of suspicion rather than the weight of fact.
lucky_guess.es: El nombre de Dunne llego a la orilla con la marea matutina como madera a la deriva — presente, plausible, pero sin probar nada por si solo. La marca de marea en sus botas, el recibo de combustible en la tienda nautica, el libro de puerto sobrescrito con tinta mas oscura: cada detalle sugeria sin confirmar. Fue acusado porque la ensenada le pertenecia y la mujer muerta habia amenazado su sustento. El mar, como siempre, no ofrecio testimonio, y el veredicto descanso en el ritmo de la sospecha mas que en el peso de los hechos.
lucky_guess.fr: Le nom de Dunne a ete rejete sur le rivage par la maree du matin comme du bois flotte — present, plausible, mais ne prouvant rien en soi. La ligne de maree sur ses bottes, le recu de carburant dans la shipchandler, le journal du port recouvert d'encre plus foncee : chaque detail suggerait sans confirmer. Il a ete inculpe parce que la crique lui appartenait et que la femme morte avait menace son gagne-pain. La mer, comme toujours, n'a offert aucun temoignage, et le verdict reposait sur le rythme du soupcon plutot que sur le poids des faits.

expressions.suspect:piers_dunne: Piers Dunne stood on the slipway with his hands in his pockets. His oilskin was dry but his boots had a tide line above the ankle.
expressions.event:tidal_window: The sea cave floods completely within forty minutes of low slack. Anyone inside without a boat would not survive the rising water.
expressions.motive:fishing_economy: The harbour depends on a fishing quota allocated by catch weight. Dunne's boats had exceeded the annual limit by three hundred tonnes.
expressions.suspect:gill_rowan: Gill Rowan crewed Dunne's lead boat and knew the cave passages. His salt-stained jacket hung in the chandlery beside a coil of new rope.
expressions.suspect:harbour_master: The harbour master signed the daily logbook and controlled slipway access. His entries for the night in question are unusually brief.
expressions.suspect:malcolm_crewe: Malcolm Crewe ran the fish market and handled the catch manifests. His fuel receipts showed a boat trip on the night of the death.
expressions.suspect:fiona_cross: Fiona Cross was the victim's sister and had argued with Dunne over access permits. Her boots carried salt from the breakwater path.
expressions.suspect:coastguard_bell: Coastguard Bell patrolled the coast path and logged vessel movements. His camera housing was found empty in the research cabin.
expressions.suspect:dr_anne_webb: Dr Anne Webb supervised the marine survey that measured fish stocks. Her report was due at the ministry by the end of the month.
expressions.location:dunne_harbour: Dunne Harbour sits in a granite cove facing west. The slipway drops steeply and the sea wall holds back spring tides.
expressions.location:sea_cave: The sea cave opens at the base of the headland and runs sixty metres inland. At low slack the floor is exposed for forty minutes.
expressions.location:fish_market: The fish market opens at five and closes when the catch is weighed. The scales are calibrated weekly and the logbook sits on the counter.
expressions.location:coast_path: The coast path follows the cliff edge from the harbour to the headland. Fog rolls in from the west without warning.
expressions.location:research_cabin: The research cabin stands on the cliff above the cave entrance. Sample jars line the shelf and a tide chart is pinned to the wall.
expressions.location:slipway: The slipway is the only launch point inside the harbour wall. The concrete is scraped by keels and the bollards hold mooring lines.
expressions.location:breakwater: The breakwater extends fifty metres from the harbour mouth. At high tide only the top course of stone is visible.
expressions.location:chandlery: The chandlery sells rope, paint, and engine parts to the fleet. A board inside the door lists the tide times for the week.
expressions.object:sample_jars: Six sample jars from the research cabin contain water from the cave. Three show elevated nitrogen levels consistent with fish waste.
expressions.object:logbook: The harbour logbook records all vessel movements by time and berth. The entry for the night of the death has been written over in darker ink.
expressions.object:mooring_rope: A mooring rope on the slipway bollard shows a clean cut six inches from the splice. The fibres indicate a sharp blade, not wear.
expressions.object:quota_records: The quota records for Dunne's fleet show annual catches within limits. An independent audit found discrepancies of three hundred tonnes.
expressions.object:water_samples: Water samples from the cave show elevated nitrogen and phosphate levels. The contamination is consistent with large-scale fish processing waste.
expressions.object:visitor_permit: Ellen Cross held a research access permit for the cave system. The permit was valid for daylight hours only.
expressions.object:engine_key: The engine key for Dunne's lead boat was found in the chandlery drawer. The ignition showed signs of recent tampering.
expressions.object:salt_stain: A salt stain on the slipway bollard extends above the normal tide line. The pattern suggests a rope was pulled tight against wet stone.
expressions.object:catch_manifest: The catch manifest for March shows three landings not recorded in the harbour logbook. The weights are listed in a different hand.
expressions.object:camera_housing: An underwater camera housing was found empty in the research cabin. The lens mount shows scratches consistent with forced removal.
expressions.object:survey_report: The marine survey report concludes that fish stocks have declined by forty percent. The decline correlates with unreported catches from Dunne's fleet.
expressions.object:fuel_receipt: A fuel receipt from the chandlery shows diesel purchased at 22:00 on the night of the death. The buyer is listed as cash.
expressions.object:anchor_chain: An anchor chain from Dunne's boat was shortened by two links. The removed links were found in the tool locker.
expressions.emotion:salt_roughness: He spoke without looking up from the rope he was coiling. His answers came in the same flat tone as the harbour wind.
expressions.emotion:steady_gaze: She held the inspector's eye without blinking for a count of five. Her hands rested on the breakwater rail.
expressions.emotion:clipped_denial: Every question about the quota was met with one word or fewer. He did not sit down during the interview.
expressions.emotion:practised_sorrow: He removed his cap and held it against his chest. His condolences were fluent and his eyes moved to the slipway.
expressions.emotion:turned_away: She turned toward the window when the survey report was mentioned. Her hand moved to the sample jars on the shelf.
expressions.emotion:hard_silence: He said nothing when shown the fuel receipt. His jaw tightened and he looked out toward the breakwater.
expressions.modifier:rope_frayed: The mooring rope was cut cleanly but the splice end showed deliberate fraying. Someone had disguised the cut as natural wear.
expressions.modifier:quota_exceeded: The independent audit found three hundred tonnes above the permitted annual catch. The excess was landed at night and sold through the market.
expressions.modifier:cave_flooded: The cave floods completely within forty minutes of low slack turning. The water rises from the back passage first.
expressions.modifier:engine_disabled: The engine ignition wire was disconnected at the starter relay. The disconnection required a spanner and knowledge of marine engines.
expressions.modifier:fog_bank: A fog bank rolled in from the west at half past three. The coast path was invisible from the harbour by four.
expressions.modifier:slipway_scraped: Fresh keel scrapes on the slipway concrete show a boat was launched between two and four in the morning. No launch was logged.
expressions.modifier:manifest_altered: The catch manifest for three landings was written in a hand that does not match the harbour master's. The ink is newer.
expressions.modifier:salt_on_jacket: Salt crystals on Dunne's oilskin jacket formed above the waterline. The pattern indicates full immersion followed by air drying.
expressions.modifier:chain_shortened: Two links were removed from the anchor chain using a bolt cutter. The cut faces show fresh steel.
expressions.modifier:boot_salt_ring: A salt ring on Fiona Cross's boots extends to mid-calf height. The ring matches the water level at the cave mouth during rising tide.
expressions.action:boat_launched: A boat was launched from the slipway between two and four in the morning. The keel scrapes are fresh and the bollard rope is slack.
expressions.action:rope_cut: The mooring rope was cut with a sharp blade close to the splice. The cut was made to look like fraying from wave action.
expressions.action:records_falsified: Three landing records were added to the catch manifest after the original entries. The ink and handwriting differ from the standard log.
expressions.action:cave_entered: Ellen Cross entered the sea cave at low slack with her sample jars. She was expected back at the research cabin within the hour.
expressions.action:engine_tampered: The engine ignition was disabled by disconnecting a single wire. The boat could not start without reconnecting it.
expressions.action:permit_revoked: Dunne attempted to revoke Ellen Cross's research permit two weeks before her death. The harbour committee overruled him.
expressions.action:samples_collected: Ellen Cross collected water samples from three points inside the cave. The nitrogen readings confirmed illegal fish waste discharge.
expressions.action:chain_released: The anchor chain was released while the boat was moored at the cave entrance. Without the chain, the boat drifted on the rising tide.
expressions.action:logbook_amended: The harbour logbook entry for the night of the death was overwritten in darker ink. The original entry is partially visible beneath.
expressions.time:low_slack: Low slack occurred at 02:14 on the morning of the death. The cave floor was exposed for approximately forty minutes.
expressions.time:rising_flood: The rising flood began at 02:54 and reached full cave height by 03:34. The water enters from the back passage first.
expressions.time:dawn_discovery: The coastguard found Ellen Cross at dawn when the tide receded. Her body was at the far end of the cave with sample jars beside her.
expressions.time:market_closing: The fish market closed at nine on the morning after the death. The catch manifest had already been filed.
expressions.time:quota_deadline: The annual quota report was due at the ministry by the end of March. The audit was triggered by Ellen Cross's preliminary findings.
expressions.motive:overfishing_cover: If the survey report reached the ministry, Dunne's fleet would lose its licence. The excess catch was worth more than the boats.
expressions.motive:survey_suppression: Ellen Cross's marine survey documented the stock decline caused by overfishing. Her data directly implicated Dunne's landing records.
expressions.motive:licence_loss: A quota violation finding would result in the revocation of all five fishing licences. The harbour economy depends on Dunne's fleet.
expressions.motive:subsidy_fraud: Malcolm Crewe received a subsidy based on reported catch volumes. If the true figures emerged, the subsidy would be clawed back.
expressions.motive:family_livelihood: Gill Rowan's family has crewed Dunne's boats for two generations. Without the fleet, the family has no income.
expressions.witness:ferry_captain: The ferry captain saw a boat heading west from the harbour at half past two. The running lights were off.
expressions.witness:bait_seller: The bait seller opened at four and saw the slipway bollard rope hanging loose. He did not report it.
expressions.witness:dock_hand: The dock hand found fresh keel scrapes on the slipway at five. He assumed a boat had launched for the early tide.
expressions.witness:pub_landlord: The pub landlord served Dunne and Crewe at nine the previous evening. They spoke quietly and left separately before closing.
expressions.witness:lifeboat_crew: The lifeboat crew was not called that night. They noted the fog bank from their station window at half past three.
expressions.event:ellen_cross_discovered: Ellen Cross was found in the sea cave at dawn with her sample jars beside her. The tide had receded and the floor was wet.
expressions.event:spring_survey: The spring survey of fish stocks was commissioned by the ministry after local reports of declining catches.
